chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
editorText:
“The drill we are about to perform is a recovery of an unconscious comrade from the vacuum of space. In the event an allies suit suffers a rupture takes a blow in space, immediately they will be subject to a potentially concussive state.”

 The suits inbuilt nanobots run on a magnetic fluid system that directs their activities in the direction of the magnetic discrepancy detected on build up amounts of iron in the blood, symbiotic of clotting, these bots can direct their energy to patch and promote coagulation in a specific area where bleed out may be occurring. A visual screen can actually be made up of the vacuum of the shell. It is from this image that the nanobots will form a bridge channeling energy to seal the void be it on the internal host or the suit. At this point we can begin the sync after the body has been stabilized. The neural bridge has a short field range of about 2000 meters, Channeling broadband synapses consume a large band of the direct channel beam,”

“But linking this to any ship will increase the range up to 50 klm” Tau didn’t rise from her seat. Merely pointed out her side of the technical designs.

”Aaah Tau while you have the floor would you please explain why the neural bridge is the safest in the field?”.. Ah yes Shai, said Tau.

“The neural bridge requires that our genetic code align. In this sense it acts as a security protocol blocking any external parties that may not be of our genetic or neural make up from Commandeering our suits and using them to their own will”.

 “Interesting” Said John, thinking deeply and discretely to himself. “So would someone half sentient be able to” John held his words and thought about how it might appear in the eyes of Athos if he continued correcting his course blocking out a full sentient takeover.

“Exactly” chuffed Tau seeming pleased with his quick resolve. You are a quick learner for a grunt”. Tau winked at John, John meeting her in kind.

“Ok.. you two stow it for the bunks hey” Shai hinted at Tau in a low voice. “This will be a full in suit drill so you will get to experience the suit in a vacuum”.

As Shai finished her sentence logistics officers escorted mag-lev crates into the room each with their own names encrypted on the crates. Tex was the first to don his suit. Walking around the room throwing hydraulically assisted punches at thin air. “Some of us will resort to our primary strengths first I see” Tex paused looking at the captain. “What” Tex stood there looking confused for a moment. “You know these suits have magnetic harpoons on them, although Tex.. They are for emergency situations only..” Said John. “Meh, I am sure I can make proper use of them”

By now the others had finished donning their Mark IV’s. The energy in the room flowed to the silent sounds of hydraulically dampened motor drives moving the suit’s hosts around the room. The sound was soft enough to be subtle yet  loud enough to be heard in close proximity. The clean architecture and smooth topography of the room made the electric and hydraulic systems sound louder than they were.

Shai made her way to the bulk head of the room on the left side veering out into the stars. John met at her side. “You ready for this Cap” she opened a one way comm channel to his suit. “Sure girl, I know I can bank on your vigilance”

At that Shai turned once again to face the others. Waiting for the logistics Engineers to wrap up and return the crates to their holding bays she began.. “Hm-Hmm So.” The rooms attention returned to Shai. “These suit’s are yours now. Your  charging locations in the launch bay will be shown in your suit’s Mapping system”, “Try not to write them off on your first walk hey guys” John smirked a little after his comment, there was a subtle seriousness in his humour.

“Now that we are all familiar with our new outfits, let’s lock in and make our way into the interlock”.As Shai finished her sentence she attended to the interlock HMI panel.

We are ready to commence interlock entry “Opening the airlock captain”. Shai held her helmet’s viewport against to the retinal scanner affixed to the Airlock door while holding her palm splayed out on the HMI. ‘Biometrics Confirmed’  pinged on the HMI overhead panel followed by an amber strobe which lit up the room around them. ‘Releasing inner Airlock Door’ pulsed intermittently. At this the door released open, hardly a sound dispersed as it’s internal pressure met the same as the training room. John entered the airlock first followed by Shai and the others in a single file. The inner airlock door was no larger than that of a fully grown male. The girls made it through with relative ease. Where the taller of the Men had to kneel down to get through particularly with the added height of the Mark IV’s the ships Engineers were yet to anticipate this minor lack of symbiotic design with ship to suit progression. The transition for each student to their holding bay was seamless, their designated seats illuminated in their Helmet’s HUD.

Tau was last to enter the airlock, closing the inner door behind her. The airlock door itself was mostly rectangular with curved corners to allow for the doors seal. Tau cranked the latch handle to the “Latched” the instructions for this clearly signed on the interlock door. “Inner door latched Captain” Said Tau, finding her seat to await blow down. The design on the interlock doors had hardly changed from the simplicity of the earlier doors aboard Cere’s in the foundation layers. While she could perform most of the actions from her suit’s interface, Shai preferred the older methods, feeling it conveyed a confidence and understanding in her colleagues that was otherwise unattainable where automation seemed to take hold.

John was busy monitoring his teams suit seal statuses ensuring that every members suit pressure readings were holding. Shai awaited John’s command . “You all know the drill” said John. “re-breathers set to %100 o2” Each member confirmed “On oxygen”, “On oxygen” one after the other, selecting their suits, blow down procedures in their on their wrist terminals as they confirmed. the Oxygen they breathed at first felt cleaner then it became colder, denser, with a metallic taste to the tongue that made you salivate.

John was still eyeing the preliminary checks before the walk, Each members suit pressure began to rise, as they did, so did their saturated oxygen, an expected bump Shai had observed.  “All vitals good captain, holding steady”, said Shai. “Suit pressure’s holding” responded John, “Checking interlock pressure seal hold” Shai resumed gleaning into the interlock HMI panel. “Seal is holding fast, both internal and external door seals”.Roger that, Shai.

“Blow down the interlock” said John “Blowing down” replied Shai. The room fell quiet with nervous anticipation eased with steady excitement. Shai looked back at John letting out a soft smile. The steel shroud of their helmets concealed any emotion, but John could feel her smiling at him. He felt confident in Shai’s abilities with the procedure.  “Airlock pressurised captain”.Shai had worked with pressure chambers regularly as part of her Deep Space Medic role which often involved treating patients for decompression illnesses from time to time at her station on Ceres before her work ethic was recognised through the chain finding it’s way to Marcellus’s ears, before she could even say goodbye to her patients she was shipped off to training and subsequently integrated into John’s team.

“Aren’t we supposed to be breathing 100% O2 for at least a day in our pods before we perform these space walks?”one of the students had posed a good question, something they hadn’t yet covered in the new suits during the training session. “You are actually correct, if it were for the older suit’s. These suits have real-time monitoring of your bloods internal nitrogen levels, and while you off-gas, your suit’s internal pressure automatically decreases to compensate and ensure minimum risk of decompression illness”

John stopped Shai for a moment, opening a private comm link between them, “Whoa whoa, you telling me they messed with the off-gassing procedure of the suits without telling us they are supposed to inform us of any of these changes that take place, if something were to happen untested we are the ones that pay dearly when we start foaming blood at the mouth” The others couldn’t hear much as most of the air had slowly been vented from the interlock removing a large portion of ability for sound to travel, all they could hear was a faint muffled mumbling reverberating to nothing, they just sat there wondering when the drill would commence and why they had been taken off comms. “Hi Captain” Kitten Chimed, you could almost hear the smile in her voice. “Records show The Mark IV testing procedures have undergone rigorous testing in according to newer heightened standards since recommendations were made by Council Senior Security Adviser Miss Ava Meerakavita under council from her board, with this ruling”, “Hey, what’s the hold up” Tex was becoming impatient interrupting John and Shai’s little meeting, “One second Tex just running some pre-walk… checks” Tex placed his palms on his knees like a toddler his elbows splayed out to the side with little regard to the space of his companions.

The others looked around the interlock at each other, John could feel the room becoming heavier as a swell of distrust and uncertainty washed over the others”

“As I was saying captain”, Kitten continued, “let’s make this quick kitten, keep it brief”. “Under this new ruling it was advised that should these.. Stricter.. testing procedures be adhered to this may save time by reducing protectant training thereby improving field deployment times of newer units as an incentive”.Kitten than finished in a conclusive tone “the following article was sent to every serving officers updates log 3 months ago”, “Oh I must have missed that one”. Kitten hadn’t been programmed to pick up on the deep sarcasm in John’s voice. “Should I continue cap?” said Shai. “Continue” said John.

“Sorry for the hold up guys”, Tex sat back folding his arms across his chest this time while Shai reassured the others. “we were just going through the new checks for the suits, as I was saying earlier” Shai began to explain as cheerfully as she had before in the training room. “The acclimatisation time in these suits is faster than the last ones, We only need to standby for 20 minutes before the walk due to the robust integrity of your new suits. We can vent while your suit maintains you at a higher off-gassing pressure,

a set group of nanobots are injected into each suit for each specific task, Your suit’s tailored nano-bots have been silently working within your blood stream to expel any and all remaining nitrogen within your blood exponentially faster than you ever naturally could.. your blood will be nitrogen free within 15 minutes”

“What about rapid decompression shouldn’t we be at the same pressure as the airlock” Tor stressed. “The internal pressure capabilities of the suit are allot higher than it’s predecessors stringent fail-safe tests carried out by the Engineers that designed it..”

Tau leant forward drawing the attention of the others cutting Shai off in the process. “What she means to say is that they have more confidence in the newer model due to it’s inbuilt kinetic response mesh, if you experience any compromise or potential rapid decompression, the suit’s shell will automatically react to the kinetic energy at the location of the compromise sealing it off” Tau finished turning her head to John sitting at the outer lock door opposite Shai.

“Guys, Allot’s changed since our last deployment, with the preparations for Europa, I understand we have had allot to take in this training session, we have had allot of downtime, but with downtime progressions have been happening in the background, If Tau trusts these progressions” John looked over to Tau, she nodded her head in kind back at him, affirming his statement. “Then I trust them.”, “If you say so cap, now can we get back to the fucking Drill”. John thought to himself. “It’s times like this I love this guy”.

“Alright then, on me, your designated stations points will be illuminated in your HUD, Find your locations on the external Hull and prepare for the recovery drill’s” . As John stood up he twisted his ankle to the left his right ankle to the right, an awkward and isolated motion at that strange enough to be a designated activation motion in isolation. his boots inbuilt mag-locks clunked to the steel deck beneath him the sound faintly knocked within the interlock dissipating amongst the few remaining air particles in the final stages of venting, as he did so an array of faint clunks could be heard as the others turned on their mag-locks behind him. As John’s Sural and tibial nerves fired in the correct sequence signifying he was lifting his foot to his suit’s neural bridge, his mag-locks released him forward slowly making his way to the outer lock latch. He grabbed onto the outer lock latch, waiting for the last of the air to vent. He took a moment to perform the final checks, voicing them as he did.

“Suit Pressures at 4.3 psi and holding..” “Check” said Tau, “Internal pressure lock sealed” “Check” Said Shai. “Suit targeting systems functional.”Check” Said Tex. “Suit fuel cells primed and charged..” “Check” Said Tau.

“Oxygen Level call outs! SOP first” The class individually called out their suit’s reserve oxygen levels.”

 “SOP Emergency Oxygen 2.. 7, 6 bar” Tex called his oxygen pressure out each number tailing the other. They all knew what unit the call outs were in. Shai followed Tex. “2, 7, 6”, then Tau, Then Tor

“2, 7” Tor paused “6” , then finished nervously.

John could see it even in his Demeanour how he sat, curled almost into a ball. It was Tor’s first time undergoing a spacewalk. It was only Marcellus’s interest in promoting him to a field Engineer that he had become subject to the more hardened rigor of the structure that followed DST training requirements. “That’s enough to get you back to the airlock if your main supply fails, will give you 30 minutes. Take your time, breath and you might get 40.”,”Ok” responded Tor, amost as nervous as before.

“Liquid cooling and ventilation systems”, “Check” Shai “All at 1.2 Liters” Shai finished with a smile.. “Heating systems” Said John. Shai’s eyes darted from her HUD to that of her teammates once more. “Check!”

Tex picked up on this “But it won’t come to that will it Cap” he said reassuringly, placing his hand on his shoulder as he sat across from Tex.  “Sure..” Said Tau, Tor still coming to wraps with the big teddy bears arm on him, not knowing to be concerned or comforted by the big guy. “We check the suits as techs before any spacewalk. Part of the procedure. The spacetrash forecast looks good. We are doing ok”,” Tau took a minute to pause checking some data on her wrist terminal.

“The last sweeper drone cleaned up about 20% so it’s clear and sunny here out no forecast for space hail honey don’t you worry!, The space walk will commence on the next day cycle. You got 45 mins of light to get setup. Thenn, we run the test on the night cycle to check the infra red tracking systems of the new suits, so don’t mess about.” “Copyy that” Tex drew his response out, he’d been here several times before and the others could tell by the annoyance in his tone.

“Full vacuum in 4, 3, 2, 1” The room fell to an almost still silence. Nothing but the sound of scrubbers filtering out Carbon dioxide from the holding bay. Then it was completely quiet. One of the cadets began to float up to the ceiling as their feet just began to lift from the grate, Tex leant down slapping the startled cadet on the calf engaging the mag locks manually. In an instant the cadet stumbled back to their feet, regaining there pasture and dignity. “Don’t mention it” he chuffed, then charged the coils on his shoulder rail cannon. “Wait this is a live fire drill” the static of the cadets comms over the dead still silence just exaggerated the unease in his voice “It will be like walking the dog in the park kid, don’t sweat”.. John looked over to Tex “you got this big guy?” “How about I just lead the class now then hey” The big man said sarcastically. He hooked his grappling hook to the rail system, gripping the release latch for the outer air lock door with his other hand in union as though he had done it several times before. Well he had, it was routine for him, being a the head mechanic. He let out a  small grunt then the hatch door popped open. He pulled himself up catching the outer hand rails on the hull as he exited, then latched his backup lanyard onto the outer rail. “I thought they updated that rail system a decade ago.” “Guess your program didn't justify overspending in the protectant budget huh” John chuckled a bit as he looked over to one of the software engineers in the class.

“We will carry out the exercise on the starboard side, away from the hatch, I don’t want any of you egg heads putting a recovery spear through the hull” John’s voice croaked as he pulled himself along the guiding rail toward the starboard pass over point. “Don’t worry, if anything goes wrong, we can send a drone out to get you”. Shai was cheerful with her remark although it did little to reassure any of the newer students.  Tau was busy setting up guy towers for the class as she recalled her time harvesting minerals around Europa “Last drones had a couple kinks with their grip strength, one guy nearly lost his leg in the Europa belt not long ago”, “Come of it Tau” chuckled Tex, “The guy was fine, just took a bit of skin off, besides the regenerative facilities on Europa I heard got an upgrade, I plan to make a private booking personally when I arrive”, “Easy big guy, can’t have you spurting anymore, The Icarus doesn’t account for big feet on over sized gorillas protectant in her holding bay” “Neither does the new mark IV have a cucumber hold” Shai laughed patting Tex on the back, “Not exactly the department I was thinking of” Tex looked over to Shai and winked. “Gross” Shai remarked “What! I only said it was for me!” Tex shrugged it off, “You guys are so sensitive” he remarked softly with a gentle tone.

“Tau I’m at the first ranging bay”, John gazed out over the hull of the Balaenoptera. The rays from the sun were blinding at first, eventually his eyes adjusted. He stood proud, for a minute illuminated just him, his shadow behind him reaching past the others, as they made out his silhouette. Tau stopped to admire him for a moment, slowing the others behind her.

“You wanna take a photo” Tex remarked. Tau reached to the starboard side and climbed up onto the next range lane with John. Looking down upon Earths surface. She could see the snow of the Himalayas on the peaks of the mountains, and she imagined how lucky they were to have such a crystal perspective above atmosphere. She stood silent absorbing the beauty of the snow belly as it stretched along the north of India like a white blanket over a waking population cooling the suns rays that would soon rest upon their villages.

“Ok I get it now” Tex made it to the next range lane, standing proud beside John and Tau. Shai was still at the back of the group, keeping checks on the rest of the class for any stragglers or.. Mishaps.

“Get the range ready Tau”,  “Roger” Tau snapped back.. “Kitten initiate mag harp turrets for backup retrieval”. A moment after Tau spoke Turrets at the rear of the training range popped out from the hull of the Balaenoptera, The turrets that had been built into the ship had become modular in their assortments, At a moments notice the Balenoptera could interchange it’s point turrets to defence rails, Emps, PDC’s, fulfilling short to medium range needs. In this case they were life recovery systems.

The larger of the ships turrets, had a grave debilitating presence, It’s shear mass could be apprehended as it’s turret spanned The entire Training range lanes alone. “When was the last intercept by the Asteroid Defence Turret Girl over there?” said Tex. Tau took a moment to let the newer recruits catch up prying deep into the range equipment's statistics. “It doesn’t show up, that’s strange, “John can we go private” Tau was holding her finger of John’s name on her wrist terminal opening a private channel, A feature she had built into her squads kit in case they’re main comms had been compromised. John looked back the last recruit straggling a bit as she came to grips with the extra pressure exerted on her body by her suits Vacuum. “Sure we got a minute, Shai, Tex… Tapping into you”.. Tor, one of the Bridge Engineers directly under Marcellus stopped for a minute observing John as he went silent. “When was Marcellus going to inform us of that, this is recent?” said Tau, “It’s Neg Vetting clearance level 2 now only from the top” said John, “Wha!?, sounds like horse manure Cap” shot Shai without hesitation.  “Yeah he’s been all up tight since this new mission came in his scope, says he needs it for disclosed tight loop activity” Said John, there was an unease to his voice.

Tau was unsettled by this, she walked out onto the range, the suns beams painting her shadow like a stalking ghost along the Balaenoptera’s hull. She poised up at the turret with uneasy eye.  “That is some Top level stuff, To think we wouldn’t even be in on that, we are told everything, I don’t like it” Taus voice was soft and hesitant “What if something goes wrong, when we are on mission, who would have the clearance to report what happens to us if Marcellus is keeping us in the dark on simple things like intercept data”.

“Ok lets keep our heads, we have a drill to complete”, said John as he veered down to the other end of the range rows. The last cadet had just made his way onto the range. “Everyone is in position, respiratory rate is up a little on the new guys, should we give them a minute to slow their breathing?”, “No” Said John softly, “There isn’t time for rest until the drill is completed. Keep the drill moving”, “Understood captain” Shai moved her fingertips along some Dials on her wrist pad. Increasing the hydration and cooling feeds to the struggling cadets. “All retrieval drones good to go” Said Tau. “You guys ready to show us how it’s done” Shai seemed chuffed she wasn’t the guinea pig this time round, Tau smiled although none of the others could see her face, they felt her knock it off like it was nothing.

John knelt down at the start of his row, clipped a Carabena off to one of the 4 fastening points in the hull and began to walk backward down the range. Each row had four fasten points one for an observer one for the trainee and spares for equipment lashing. Tau knelt down in the same row as John fastening herself on a free slot. She turned about face and observed John as he lowered himself down around the hull, steadily one magboot after the other. The process felt like it took forever, despite how well the muscle pickups in the mag boots actuated their coils in sync with the user. “Enjoying the walk in the park their Cap” Tex joked, “Maybe you can bring your dog next time?”. “You can write the letter to the loved ones of the cadet that gets lost at space when they get lost from trying to do it like the real cowboys do” Tex felt John winking at him in his tone from behind his visor. “Fair point, although I’m not the poetic type… so slow is smooth, smooth is fast right” “Roger that” croaked John. “I’m Just about in position for release”, “Ok cap, I’m ready to commence the neural sever on your mark”, “Wait till I’m at 80% of the retrieval limit”, “Huh?  Isn’t that pushing it a bit”, “Tau ?” John checked to see how confident she was with the neural bridge. “Lock it in” said Tau without hesitation. “Ok 80% neural bridge set” said Shai.

 "The ships correctional thrusts  will be temporarily disabled  once I commence the drill, I should match the ships trajectory so long as she doesn’t veer of course”. John was busy tapping away on his wrist terminal “Lets showem how it’s done shall we”

John reached down to engage the bypass on his mag boots. Both feet at the same time began to lift from the Baelenoptera’s hull, He watched on breathing calmly as he observed the reel mounted to the hull, spew out meter after meter of rope, easing him out to a mere blip in the suns rays looking back down upon the others. He felt a sense of calm floating in space, earthed to nothing, without worries or commitment here out, he felt his mind drift through time and space.

“Ok..” Shai honed her focus. “I have him at 75% Tau are you ready for the bridge?” “Roger” Tau looked over to shai with an affirming nod. John felt his connection to the suit sever, his vitals showing a blank feed accross his HUD, the word “Nueral Intercept Activating fed accross his feed”  He felt his mind drifting and then, in an instant he felt himself earthed again. He looked back at his body floating through space. He could still feel his own movements, his feet firmly locked to the hull, although they weren’t his feet, they were Tau’s and she was looking straight back at him through his neural feed.

“This always makes me a little squeamish” said Tau. Adjusting and reorienting herself to the retrieval point. “How’s it feel being in my head” John joked. “It wouldn’t surprise me if I wasn’t there most of the time” Tau joked back. “Get a room!” Tex was getting tired watching them have all the fun. “You aren’t exactly in his head Tau..” Shai intervened. “The suit is simply transmitting your synapses and visual feedback between one another, It just feels real because well, that’s just how good the nervous system in the Mark IV is”, John Cut Shai off  “Thanks for the fun facts Shai, How’s that lock looking Tau”… Tau was silent, gleaning at the target “Account for the bridge delay” Tau thought to herself “Wait they patched the delay in the new suit.. Did they..” She questioned herself, as a nervous sweat began to track down her forehead. John could see Tau’s reflection ever so faintly on the internal wall of her visor, as he watched his retrieval range come closer to it’s limit nearing 85%. “I have a lock, go back to sleep John” She brushed off her doubts, locked the trajectory and actuated John’s suit thrusters for a slight pivot left. She watched on anxiously as the DZ entered the middle of her suits targeting  reticle.

Without announcement a crisp ejection of air erupted from   just above the hip of John’s suit. A tethered harpoon no larger than a 50 cal round silently but rapidly unfoiled a tether behind it, making it’s way right on point of the DZ. Before hitting the hull, a proximity sensor fitted within the harpoon actuated reverse thrust chambers berried within the harpoon. It so gently coupled with the hull locking in place, it’s tip all within half a second had mag locked and then welded itself to the hull through. “Thank Fuck for our Engineers huh” Said Tau, “I have you ready for retrieval Cap” John looked up at his body drifting in space his arms proud above his head both thumbs up, Tau looking back at him, she watched as her head nodded in approval back at her.

There was something surreal about seeing yourself look back at you, although she knew deep down it was all puppet work by the suits. Acting like Caddies, the suits became neural messengers and actuators, While it was nice to imagine a world where humans might one day trade bodies in the flesh she knew it wasn’t as real as it seemed.

Tex looked on pondering for a moment of all the fun things he might do if it were, of the flesh. Shai however knew it was all show and focused on the neural bridge statistics blazened across her helmet visor. Synapse delays, Autonomous system filters ensuring any sound from incoming motor functions that didn’t match the wearers profile didn’t send their breathing into arrythmia, or their muscles to spasm. All of these things still needed attention and while the Engineers had done there best to filter out the knooks and bumps through bi directional biological sample filters. The system was relatively new, and the Neural loop needed to be carefully monitored for any drastic evolvements.

“Alright let’s bring me back” said John, watching himself now being dragged along by the what felt like the ships gravity.

Tau pressed a small recessed panel on her suit above the harpoon bay, the panel recessed into her suit revealing a small two directional toggle, “In”, “Out” displayed ether side of it.

Tau pressed her finger down on the toggle. John watched on as the sillouhette of his body became increasingly larger being drawn back to the ship. Tex was on the controls of the backup tether matching the retrieval speed so both lines didn’t become tangled. It all seemed a bit much to Tex, cumbersome. Although he understood training controls needed to be in place despite how many space walks his squad had carried out over a generation. It didn’t take long for John’s suit reel to have him a few dozen meters from the hull.

Tau, eyed the approach anticipating the landing, she rose John’s knees ever so slightly to absorb the landing. As John’s body touched down, he toppled forward a touch, Tau losing balance over the added weight of the captain. “Whoa, there, you’ve gained some weight I see!” said Tau, startled she collected her balance. John’s mag-boots automatically re-engaged, locking him to the surface of the hull.

“Closing out the bridge” Said Shai. John and Tau felt everything go dark for a few milliseconds, then they were back in their suits, breathing in their own bodies. “Fuck that feels stranger everytime we do that” said John. “Yeah, the synapse response delay is almost unnoticiable now, It’s almost as ifyou aren’t just driving another suit anymore” .

The other cadets stood by waiting for their turns. John collected himself after the demonstration for a moment. Then made his way down the range checking each cadets tether. He opened a private channel to Shai “How we looking on neural bridge compatibility, any hiccups?”, “We are all good to go Cap”, “Good, Lady Ava has requested my attention after the drill, So let’s wrap this up and keep it clean”, “You bet ya cap!” Said Shai confidently. Moments later the shadows of several cadets scattered accross the range as they floated beside the Baelenoptra in what felt like to those still mag locked to the hull, like metal birds in an empty sky, with earths atmosphere as the backdrop. While to the newer cadets the experience was one they would remember for generation, John and his team were already accounting for their kit maintenance in their minds for the next drop. It was nothing new to them, but even still they took a moment to appreciate beautiful uncoordinated chaos of a small group floating in space suspended along the side a sleeping giant in a deep vast ocean of emptiness.

The quiet stillness of the moment was short lived. The comms channel became overwhelmed with gargled static followed by a lingering suspicion amongst Shai and the others as they exchanged glances between one another.

“Aaah, looks like one of the cadets vomited in their helmet again” Shai was monitoring the feeds when she came accross what looked like a failed painting of pinks and greens smeared accross the visor. “There’s always one, I’d personally just blame it on the salmon” Tex was talking to the cadet with comforting words as he wandered over to the bay and started the retrieval tether. The cadet dangled disoriented and confused as he slowly made his way back down to the range.

Shai felt bad for the technicians. She knew they had it hard enough as it was with the state they often returned their equipment in after a deployment.

“Hmmph well, I guess they haven’t eased out all the neural bridge kinks just yet… Maybe an incentive could be getting the Engineers to clean the helmets before the tech services after each drill”.

“Agreed Siante” Said John. “Although a bit of vomit in the helmet is a big leap from soiling your suit liner, having proper control of your bowels this time round is a plus”.

Tex was leaning against the retrieval lever as knoding in agreeance. “Yeaahh, synaptic bowel muscle malfunction or something along those lines was the official report”, Shai cut Tex off  “Didn’t that kid give you shit for failing one of your Star Nav courses or something”, Tex directed his comms channel to Tau Shai and John alone “Nobody liked that kid anyway.. You think they would court marshal me if it was intentional?”.. Shai’s face was ridden with disgust “You mean to tell us that you bridged with that kid, and soiled his suit just before the sever?” Tex took a moment to think on his response. “Well technically speaking it was him that soiled his suit”, “Remind me to never upset Tex on a training drill, especially on Tuesdays”, “I .. love  .. curry night” Tex concurred on the open channel, the rest of the cadets went on with the drill confused coming half way into their conversation.

“Tau, can you wrap up here with the new recruits, I’ve got to head back”. John was looking down at his wrist terminal as an Amber notification strobed accross it’s screen “Incoming hail from Ava Marakaveeta” blinked with the usual high priority Protectant flag on the end of the notification for urgent effect. “I’ve got Ava on my back again, politics right..” John closed out the notification, disconnected his tether from the range and started a blow down sequence on one of the spare airlocks to make his way back into the ship.

“”
